newsitem.title: USA: U.S. nonfarm payrolls seen staying strong in June.
newsitem.headline: U.S. nonfarm payrolls seen staying strong in June.

text.p: Continued strength in the U.S. labor market was expected to be seen in the June nonfarm payrolls report scheduled for release on Thursday, economists said.

Analysts polled by Reuters expected, on average, that payrolls would grow by 222,000 in the month as the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.8 percent. They also saw average hourly earnings rising by 0.4 percent and the average workweek rising to 34.6 hours from 34.5 hours in the prior month.
Jerry Zukowski, economist at PaineWebber Inc, expected payrolls would rise by 285,000 in the month.
However, Zukowski said his estimate did not portend a sharp rise in payrolls, but was due to seasonal factors. Nonetheless, the U.S. labor market remained tight, he said.
"The only thing to slow (the labor market) would be the inability of firms to find workers," Zukowski said.
Peter Kretzmer, senior economist at Nationsbanc Capital Markets Inc, said the labor market seemed to be weakening somewhat, though it remained very strong.
He cited a drop in the Conference Board's help wanted index and some signals that demand was slowing.
"(The labor market) clearly remains on the tight side. Service spending has been very good" and service employment should remain healthy as a result, Kretzmer said.
He looked for nonfarm payrolls to grow by 170,000, which is well below concensus estimates, yet still would represent a solid gain, he said.
"It's difficult to find the workers businesses are looking for," Kretzmer said. He said it was difficult for firms to hire workers as profit margins were a constraining influence currently.
